conclusion: The 10k one-model outcome is a global growth/initialization divergence, not a boundary triangulation issue: the port's initial pair and subsequent registration order differ fundamentally from COLMAP's, producing one connected component. This supersedes the boundary-specific triangulation hypothesis (PR #164/#165/#171).
findings: The port's registration order diverges drastically from COLMAP's: the port registers frame 4497 at num_reg_frames=4995 (near the end; snapshot points3d=134711), whereas COLMAP's model0 registers image #9497 at num_reg_frames=4493.

At num_reg_frames ~4488-4491 the port's boundary frames 4493-4505 all report num_visible_points3d=0, exactly like COLMAP's model0 end state. So the port's local frontier also stalls at the boundary; it then continues registering other (far-side) frames and eventually covers all 5000 frames in a single component.

The port's initial pair is frames 388/420 (cam1) after an earlier trial pair 3181/3213; COLMAP's model0 initial pair is image #5446/#5463 = rig/camera2 names at t=18.390/18.923 = flat cam2_000893/cam2_000925 = frames 446/462 (cam2). Forcing the port to use the COLMAP pair (port image ids 5446/5462 or cam1 446/462) is rejected: initialize_reconstruction returns NoInitialPair and the run keeps 0 models.
method: Added an env-gated boundary snapshot (VISLOC_SNAPSHOT_AFTER_FRAME=4497 + VISLOC_SNAPSHOT_DIR) and reran 10k with VISLOC_DEBUG_BOUNDARY_FRAMES=4493..4505, MIN_REG=4488.
